commentKey.description: The set `threads` belong to; it switches when the reviewer focuses another slice.

threads.description: Threads changed since the cursor, as they are now; after a key switch or a resync, every thread of the set.

removed.description: Ids of threads changed since the cursor that no longer exist.

resync.description: The cursor came from another run or fell out of the log's window: `threads` is the full set.

closed.description: The server is closing; nothing more will come.

Activity.description: What changed in the shown comment set since a cursor.

ignore.description: An author whose changes do not end the wait; they are still reported once something else does.

AuthorQuery.description: Who deletes, on `DELETE` of a thread or a message. Absent: the reviewer.

time.description: Author time, in seconds since the epoch.

BlameCommit.description: A commit that last changed some blamed lines.

start.description: 1-based first line on the blamed side.

commit.description: A `commits` entry's sha; null for worktree lines no commit holds yet.

BlameHunk.description: Consecutive lines one commit last changed.

start.description: 1-based first line to blame; the whole side when absent.

end.description: 1-based last line, inclusive; `start` alone blames that one line.

BlameRequest.description: `POST /api/blame`: who last changed lines of one side of a file, read through the allowlist `/api/file` reads.

hunks.description: In line order, covering the requested lines that exist.

BlameResponse.description:
A side is blamed at its own commit, so in a range a line the range added names its commit there;
the worktree is blamed against HEAD. A side with no history, as an interdiff's replayed old side, is a 404.

path.description: New path (or old path for deletions).

blob.description: New-side blob sha. '' for deletions. Keys the viewed state.

oldBlob.description: Old-side blob sha. '' for additions. A worktree side's blob, like `blob`, is '' when the file cannot be hashed.

generated.description: The `linguist-generated` gitattribute, a path pattern or a content sniff said this file is generated. Feeds auto-collapse and risk ranking.

submodule.description: A gitlink (mode 160000): `blob` is the recorded commit, the patch shows the commit-id change, and there is no file to open.

side.description: Column the user selected in a diff; 'new' for file items.

quoted.description: Exact text of [startLine, endLine] at creation.

oneOf.description: A thread on a line range of one side.

path.description: The changed file's path (its new path for a rename), or any tree path.

oneOf.description: A thread on a file as a whole, with no line: GitHub's file-level comment.

CommentAuthor.description: Who wrote a message that the reviewer did not: only `diffle comments` sends it, never the browser.

messages.description: At least one; [0] opened the thread.

stale.description: Relocation failed after a snapshot refresh: the lines left the diff, or the file left the review.

staleFromLine.description: Original startLine of a line thread, shown in export when stale.

CommentThread.description: A conversation anchored to a line range or a whole file. The thread owns the anchor; replies follow it.

ComparisonBase.description: How a range's old side is derived: `old` itself, or merge-base(old, new) with the worktree taken as HEAD.

ConfigUpdate.description: Writable HTTP config fields; unknown keys, including CLI-only lspCommands and githubHosts, are stripped.

EnterRequest.description:
What the CLI and the picker enter a review with: the words, parsed and resolved by the server
into a `Review`. A slice of the active range is chosen with a `RangeView` instead.

path.description: The changed file's path (its new path for a rename), or any tree path.

FileAnchor.description: A thread on a file as a whole, with no line: GitHub's file-level comment.

FollowRefs.description:
How a review between refs reacts when one of them moves. `on`: recompute at once, as a worktree
review follows edits. `off`: announce the move and wait for Reload. `auto`: wait for Reload when an
endpoint names a branch, whose pushes and rebases should not swap the review out under the
reviewer; recompute at once otherwise (a detached HEAD, a tag, an expression).

GithubExportRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/github/export`. Without `threadIds`, every unresolved thread of the mode.

url.description: The pull request whose pending review the comments joined; the human submits the review there.

posted.description: Review comments added to the pending review.

updated.description: Comments already in the pending review at the same anchor whose body this call rewrote in place.

review.description: Whether this call opened the pending review or added to one that was already waiting.

skipped.description: Threads left out, with why (stale, resolved, unknown id, an identical comment already in the review).

version.description: Snapshot.version used for this lookup; the client discards results for a different snapshot version.

repository.description: GitHub repository identified by the local origin URL.

repositoryUrl.description: Its page, on whichever GitHub the run talks to.

reason.description: Null when export is allowed; otherwise explains why it is blocked.

GithubMetadata.description: Optional enrichment for a snapshot, independent of its comparison.

lines.description: Lines in `from`'s file holding those references, ascending.

GraphEdge.description: `from` uses `to`: the language server lists places inside `from` among `to`'s references.

kind.description: LSP SymbolKind number; the client maps it to a label.

container.description: Enclosing class or function, when any.

line.description: Line of the name, where navigation lands.

startLine.description: First line of the declaration's full range, before `line` when a decorator or doc comment leads it.

endLine.description: Last line of the declaration's full range.

id.description: `path:line:col` of the symbol's name, or the path of a file-level consumer. Stable within a snapshot.

moreConsumers.description: Consumers left out beyond the per-symbol cap; changed symbols only.

GraphNodeStatus.description: A changed symbol carries its change; a `consumer` is unchanged code that uses one.

GraphQuery.description:
`GET /api/lsp/graph`: `all` lifts the cap on changed symbols; `scope`, a folder without its
trailing slash, graphs only the changed files under it, whose dependents may live anywhere.

cut.description: Changed symbols past the server's cap, by whole files, most telling first; drawn with `GraphQuery.all`.

inconclusive.description: Why the graph may lack nodes or edges: a server was busy or unavailable while answering.

GraphResponse.description: `GET /api/lsp/graph`: the snapshot's changed symbols and the code using them, from the language servers.

language.description: The grammar's name, e.g. `Rust`. Null when none matched or the side is binary or too large to highlight; `lines` is empty then.

lines.description: Tokens per line, first line first. Highlighting stops at a time limit, so a long side may have fewer entries than lines: the rest are plain.

HighlightResponse.description:
`GET /api/highlight` (a `FileQuery`): one side of a file as syntax tokens, read as `/api/file` reads it.
Highlighting the whole side keeps multi-line strings and comments right in a hunk.

ImageQuery.description:
`GET /api/image`: one side of a file as image bytes. The server answers 404 unless `key` is that side's
`imageKey` in its current snapshot, the bytes are still the ones the key names, and they are a raster image.

pairs.description: The two ranges' commits paired, in `git range-diff` order: the newer range's, dropped commits where they were.

conflicts.description: Paths the shown replay could not merge; they carry conflict markers on the old side.

Interdiff.description: An interdiff view as the snapshot resolved it: the two ranges' commits and their pairing.

Iteration.description:
One state of a reviewed range: its resolved endpoints when a snapshot of it was taken. A new
one is recorded whenever the endpoints differ from the last, so a push, rebase or amend
yields the next iteration; the commits are pinned under `refs/diffle/iterations/`.

LanguageId.description:
A language diffle can start a server for. The value is the LSP `languageId` the
server is told in `didOpen`, so it must be the spec's spelling, not ours.

LastCommitsPreview.description: Endpoints of HEAD~oldOffset..HEAD~newOffset, resolved against the same HEAD. Null means the commit does not exist.

side.description: Column the user selected in a diff; 'new' for file items.

quoted.description: Exact text of [startLine, endLine] at creation.

LineAnchor.description: A thread on a line range of one side.

Live.description: What a snapshot follows: the worktree, the refs the range was named by, or nothing (pinned hashes, a pull request, an interdiff).

LspFeature.description:
A request the bridge sends a server only once it advertised the capability, in its
`initialize` result or by registering it later, as an editor does. Document highlights
are advisory: without them the answer is empty, never an error.

LspHoverRequest.description:
`POST /api/lsp/hover`. `ownerOnly` asks the file's own server alone: a server joining the
language, such as Tailwind's, adds notes for markup that read as noise on a declaration.

contents.description: Markdown; null when the server has nothing for the position.

range.description: The span the contents describe, when the server says. Same units as LspPosition.

LspHoverResponse.description: What the language server says about a position, for the hover tooltip.

text.description: The target line's text, for result lists.

external.description:
The file is not in the snapshot (stdlib, site-packages, an ignored venv) and `path` is absolute.
`/api/file` serves it on the new side, read-only, and the servers that named it answer queries from it,
for as long as they keep naming it.

LspLocationsResponse.description: Results the server could place: snapshot paths, or files it read from disk on the language server's word.

seq.description: Changes whenever a line is added or repeated, so a reader showing the log knows to fetch again.

errors.description: Error and warning lines since the server started, kept or not.

id.description: Stable identity of the line within the run.

time.description: Milliseconds since the epoch, of its latest repeat.

count.description: How many times in a row the server said exactly this.

LspLogEntry.description: One line of a server's output channel. The bridge keeps a bounded number of recent ones.

LspLogQuery.description: `GET /api/lsp/log?server=<command>`: the retained lines of one server, oldest first.

LspLogSource.description: Where a log line came from: `window/showMessage`, `window/logMessage`, or the process's stderr.

tried.description: Programs looked for on PATH, so the UI can name what to install. Empty when config turned the language off.

why.description:
A program that is on PATH but lacks what the server loads from beside it, such as a
`vue-language-server` without its tsserver plugin: installing more is not the answer.

LspMissing.description: A language in the diff with no server behind it.

kind.description: LSP DocumentHighlightKind: a plain textual match, a read, or a write.

LspOccurrence.description: One place a symbol occurs in its own file, from `textDocument/documentHighlight`. Same units as LspPosition.

LspOccurrencesResponse.description: Every occurrence of the symbol at a position in the same file; empty when the server has none or no opinion.

LspPosition.description: A point in a new-side file. LSP semantics: the column counts UTF-16 units, like a JS string index.

name.description: Program name, for messages: the basename of the command's first word, e.g. `pyrefly`.

command.description: The command line it was started from.

state.description: `ready` means initialized; LSP has no universal workspace-ready signal.

activity.description: Active work reported through LSP work-done progress; absent when none is reported.

notice.description:
What the server last said to the reader through `window/showMessage`, when it was a
warning or an error. Its log never stands here: that is `log`.

log.description: The server's output channel in brief; `GET /api/lsp/log` lists the lines.

label.description: What it was pointed at, e.g. `TypeScript 5.9.3` or `Cargo workspaces`.

paths.description: Repository-relative, else `~`-abbreviated or absolute. Empty when nothing was found.

LspProjects.description: Where diffle pointed a server, found from the diff's files: which project's code it reads.

name.description: Program name, for messages: the basename of the command's first word, e.g. `pyrefly`.

command.description: The command line it was started from.

state.description: `ready` means initialized; LSP has no universal workspace-ready signal.

activity.description: Active work reported through LSP work-done progress; absent when none is reported.

notice.description:
What the server last said to the reader through `window/showMessage`, when it was a
warning or an error. Its log never stands here: that is `log`.

log.description: The server's output channel in brief; `GET /api/lsp/log` lists the lines.

languages.description: Languages it owns: asked first, and alone for highlights, token kinds and outlines.

joins.description: Languages it answers for beside their owner, such as Tailwind's class hovers in markup.

supports.description: What its `initialize` result advertised; empty while starting.

projects.description: Absent for a server diffle points at no project.

LspServerStatus.description: A process plus the languages the pool routes to it.

LspState.description: One language server process, as its bridge sees it.

enabled.description: False with `--no-lsp`: no server will start for this run.

servers.description: One entry per started server. Empty until a snapshot names a language with a server on PATH.

kind.description: LSP SymbolKind number; the client maps it to a label.

container.description: Enclosing class or function, when any.

line.description: Line of the name, where navigation lands.

startLine.description: First line of the declaration's full range, before `line` when a decorator or doc comment leads it.

endLine.description: Last line of the declaration's full range.

LspSymbolsResponse.description: `GET /api/lsp/symbols`: a file's outline with `path`, else the repository's symbols matching `q`.

version.description: The snapshot a reload would supersede.

oldSha.description: Where the comparison `Snapshot.commits` spans resolves now.

Moved.description:
The compared refs resolve elsewhere than when the shown snapshot was taken. A refs-live
comparison is not recomputed under the reviewer; it reloads on request.

PairStatus.description: How a commit of the older iteration relates to one of the newer, as `git range-diff` pairs them.

PatchRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/patch`: the changed files whose patches to return, concatenated. Unknown paths are skipped.

reason.description: Why there is no link: no forge origin, the worktree, a review that changed, an unpushed commit.

Permalink.description:
A link to lines at the commit their side shows, judged from local refs alone (no token, no
network, no cache, so a push shows on the next request), or why there is none.

version.description: Snapshot.version the lines were read from; another one is refused with a reason.

path.description: The changed file's path; an old-side link follows a rename to its old path.

PermalinkRequest.description: Lines of one side of a snapshot to link to on the forge origin points at.

headRepository.description: `owner/name` of the head repository; null when it was deleted.

PullRef.description: The pull request a range was entered as: its identity, which keys its comments and names its export target.

RangeCommit.description: One commit of the compared range.

list.description: Oldest first; the newest MAX_RANGE_COMMITS when there are more.

oldSha.description: The spanned range's resolved endpoints: the snapshot's own when it shows the whole range.

RangeCommits.description:
The commits the review's range spans: old..new, with the worktree taken as HEAD; a lone commit lists itself.
Every slice of a range lists the range's.

RangePair.description:
One row of a range-diff: `identical` and `changed` pairs have both commits, a `message` pair
the same patch under a new message, an `added` commit no old side and a `dropped` one no new side.

RangeRef.description: One side of an interdiff: a recorded iteration of the range, or a range the reviewer named, `old..new`.

RangeView.description:
Which slice of a range is on screen. The range's commits stay listed whatever is shown.
- `whole`: the range itself.
- `commit`: one listed commit against its first parent.
- `uncommitted`: the uncommitted changes of a range that ends at the worktree.
- `interdiff`: what `to` (the range as it is now when absent) changed since `from`: `from`'s
  head replayed onto `to`'s base against `to`'s head, so a rebase in between does not show up
  as the upstream's changes. With `pair`, one pair of the two ranges' commits by its new-side
  hash: that commit against its old self replayed onto its parent, or against its parent when added.

author.description: Absent: the reviewer resolves or reopens.

Review.description:
What is under review, as named: a range between two revisions (either may be "worktree"), with
the slice of it on screen, or one commit against its first parent. Nothing here is resolved:
the snapshot carries the hashes, what the review follows and where its comments live.

parent.description: First parent; null for a root commit.

child.description: The commit whose first parent this is, toward HEAD; null at HEAD or off HEAD's first-parent line.

ReviewedCommit.description: A single reviewed commit and its neighbours along HEAD's first-parent history, for stepping through it.

SearchContent.description: Whether search includes whole files or only new-side diff hunks and their context.

SearchScope.description: Where `/api/search` looks: one file (`path`), the diff's changed files (default), or the whole new-side tree.

gitDir.description: The repository's git directory, as the server resolved it.

version.description: The server's semantic version, as `diffle --version` prints it.

label.description: The active review's comparison label, as the run's status line names it; absent until the first review resolves.

ServerInfo.description:
What `GET /api/server` answers, before the first review resolves too: which run is listening, for
which repository. A client trusts `<git-dir>/diffle/server.json` only when its `instance` and
`gitDir` match this.

cursor.description: After the change this announces; `GET /api/threads/activity` takes it as `since`.

version.description: Monotonic; bumps on every refresh and mode switch.

oldSha.description: Resolved endpoints; either can be the worktree sentinel. An interdiff's old side is a replayed tree.

headSha.description: The checked-out commit; '' on an unborn branch. Symbol navigation needs newSha to be this or the worktree.

follows.description: What the review follows: worktree edits recompute it, moved refs announce themselves, nothing for pinned sides.

commentKey.description:
Where the review's threads and viewed marks live: fixed by what was entered, never by
discovery, so they survive pushes. An interdiff keeps viewed marks under a key of its own,
but takes no new threads: its old side is a replayed tree the range never shows again.

interdiff.description: Set for an interdiff view: how it was resolved.

context.description: Context lines the patches were generated with.

tree.description: All paths on the new side: the new commit's tree, or index ∪ untracked for the worktree. Sorted.

commit.description: The shown commit, with its neighbours: a lone commit, a focused one, or an added commit of an interdiff pair; otherwise null.

iterations.description: The recorded iterations of the range `commits` spans, oldest first; empty for comparisons that are not followed.

author.description: Absent: the reviewer opens the thread.

ThreadCreate.description:
Create payload. Without `startLine` the thread is on the file as a whole; then `side`,
`endLine` and `quoted` are refused rather than ignored, so a payload that meant a line
never lands on the file. `quoted` is optional: the server quotes the range from the snapshot.

commentKey.description: The set the threads belong to: `Snapshot.commentKey` of the slice shown when they were read.

ThreadList.description: What `GET /api/threads` answers: the threads of the set the reviewer is shown, read under one key.

Token.description: A token on one line. Columns count UTF-16 units, like a JS string index; `end` is exclusive. Text outside every token is plain.

TokenKind.description: What a highlighted token is, from its grammar's scopes; each client picks the colors.

version.description: The `Snapshot.version` the tour was checked against when pushed.

Tour.description: The review's tour: one HTML document, as the agent last pushed it.

kind.description: `note` for context, `warning` for a risk the reviewer should check.

TourCallout.description: A highlighted aside inside a card. It holds what a card holds, except another callout.

id.description: Unique in the tour; edges name it. Letters, digits, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter.

step.description: Its place in the walk (`1`, `2`, ...), unique; the reviewer steps through cards in this order. Without one, the card is context.

title.description: The heading the card and the step outline show.

TourCard.description:
A box of prose and primitives, and a node on the canvas. It sits at the top level or in a
`diffle-group`, and holds plain tags, `diffle-diff`, `diffle-tree`, `diffle-jump`,
`diffle-symbol` and `diffle-callout`. Keep it short: a title, a sentence or two, and one diff.

path.description: A file of the review, relative to the repository root; a renamed file by its new path.

side.description: Which side's line numbers `lines` counts: `old` (before) or `new` (after, the default).

lines.description: The line range on that side, `40-58`, or one line, `40`.

TourDiff.description: Lines of the review's diff, highlighted, with a jump to them. It holds nothing.

to.description: The card the arrow points at.

label.description: A few words on the arrow: what flows along it.

TourEdge.description: An arrow from one card to another, at the top level. It holds nothing: close it with `</diffle-edge>`.

id.description: Unique in the tour; edges name it. Letters, digits, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter.

step.description: Its place in the walk (`1`, `2`, ...), unique; the reviewer steps through cards in this order. Without one, the card is context.

title.description: The heading the card and the step outline show.

oneOf.description:
A box of prose and primitives, and a node on the canvas. It sits at the top level or in a
`diffle-group`, and holds plain tags, `diffle-diff`, `diffle-tree`, `diffle-jump`,
`diffle-symbol` and `diffle-callout`. Keep it short: a title, a sentence or two, and one diff.

title.description: What the cards in it have in common.

oneOf.description: A frame around related cards (a layer, a package), at the top level. It holds `diffle-card`s only.

to.description: The card the arrow points at.

label.description: A few words on the arrow: what flows along it.

oneOf.description: An arrow from one card to another, at the top level. It holds nothing: close it with `</diffle-edge>`.

path.description: A file of the review, relative to the repository root; a renamed file by its new path.

side.description: Which side's line numbers `lines` counts: `old` (before) or `new` (after, the default).

lines.description: The line range on that side, `40-58`, or one line, `40`.

oneOf.description: Lines of the review's diff, highlighted, with a jump to them. It holds nothing.

paths.description: Files of the review, one per line, relative to the repository root.

root.description: The folder the tree starts at, without a trailing `/`; every path lies under it. Default: the repository root.

oneOf.description: A directory tree of some files; changed ones show their status. It holds nothing.

path.description: A file of the review, relative to the repository root.

line.description: The line to land on; without it, the file's first change.

side.description: Which side `line` counts on: `old` or `new` (the default).

oneOf.description: A button that opens the diff view at a file or a line. Its text is the label; empty, it shows `path:line`.

path.description: A file of the review, relative to the repository root.

name.description: The symbol, exactly as it appears on that line.

side.description: Which side `line` counts on: `old` or `new` (the default).

oneOf.description: A chip for a symbol on a line; it opens the language server's references to it. It holds nothing.

kind.description: `note` for context, `warning` for a risk the reviewer should check.

oneOf.description: A highlighted aside inside a card. It holds what a card holds, except another callout.

TourElement.description: A `diffle-*` element of a tour with its attributes, which are strings as in HTML.

element.description: The culprit as the document spells it, with the card it sits in: `diffle-card#auth > diffle-diff path="a.rs"`.

TourError.description: One reason a pushed tour was refused.

title.description: What the cards in it have in common.

TourGroup.description: A frame around related cards (a layer, a package), at the top level. It holds `diffle-card`s only.

path.description: A file of the review, relative to the repository root.

line.description: The line to land on; without it, the file's first change.

side.description: Which side `line` counts on: `old` or `new` (the default).

TourJump.description: A button that opens the diff view at a file or a line. Its text is the label; empty, it shows `path:line`.

TourRejection.description: What `PUT /api/tour` answers with 422: every reason, in document order.

TourResponse.description: `GET /api/tour`: the review's tour, or null without one.

path.description: A file of the review, relative to the repository root.

name.description: The symbol, exactly as it appears on that line.

side.description: Which side `line` counts on: `old` or `new` (the default).

TourSymbol.description: A chip for a symbol on a line; it opens the language server's references to it. It holds nothing.

TourTag.description:
The plain tags a tour may use inside cards, for prose and structure. They take no attributes,
except `a`, which takes an `href` to an `http(s)` URL.

paths.description: Files of the review, one per line, relative to the repository root.

root.description: The folder the tree starts at, without a trailing `/`; every path lies under it. Default: the repository root.

TourTree.description: A directory tree of some files; changed ones show their status. It holds nothing.

autoViewed.description: Globs (picomatch syntax) for files that start viewed + collapsed. Empty by default.

contextLines.description: Unchanged lines shown around each change (git -U). Default 5.

followRefs.description: When a review between refs recomputes as its refs move; see `FollowRefsSchema`. Default auto.

lineWrap.description: Wrap long lines in the viewer instead of scrolling them sideways. Default true.

lspCommands.description:
Language server command per language, replacing the built-in candidate for it; an empty
string disables the language. Read-only over HTTP; set in the config file, whose path `diffle config` prints.

githubHosts.description:
GitHub Enterprise hosts: the host in remote urls → the host serving the web UI and API, the
same one for most. github.com needs no entry. Read-only over HTTP; set by editing the
config file.

ViewedEntry.description: Explicit viewed/unviewed mark for a path at a specific new-side content.

ViewedState.description: Derived per changed file: 'restale' means viewed at an older blob.
